﻿Reproduced on integration head b7a8c9ddac in src/ui/room-template-world-bridge.ts.

Press/release to place a room plan, hold the placement-port confirmation pending, move the cursor to a different tile, then accept the placement. The room is accepted but the tool remains armed because the hover query increments the same request revision used to filter the committed placement response. This can invite unintended repeated placement.

A focused production-path regression fails: expected tool.isArmed() false, received true. Expected: the accepted command disarms its original tool even if the preview moved. A newly armed/selected tool must still be protected from an older confirmation, and a stale refusal must not repaint a newer preview. Fix in progress, no save or player-copy change.

comments.body: ﻿Fix pushed on the full integration branch. A delayed accepted placement now disarms its original selection even if hover queries moved forward. The revision check still protects newly armed selections, and refusals are painted only for the current preview. Regression red before; eleven bridge/tool tests and TypeScript green after. Draft PR #1899 retains the full integration, pending unrelated owner save-format approval and runtime release gates.

## Source-confirmed extension: renderer replacement also superseded matching accepted completion

Fresh complete body/comment review shows this is the same bridge accepted-receipt ownership surface as #1908, so no duplicate Issue is opened. #1681 protects a newly selected angled revision; #1967 owns option navigation during renderer preparation. This reproduction keeps the tool revision unchanged.

Actual main deactivate/changed callbacks, real LiveRendererSelection, RoomTemplateTool and WorldBridge pointer listeners reproduce both World->Angled and Angled->World: pointerdown/up starts placement, its port confirmation stays pending, renderer replacement disposes the old bridge, accepted confirmation then arrives. The shared original tool stays armed because disposed is in the completion early return. Normal accepted placement stands down.

Source baseline:2 RED /6 controls GREEN,579ms. Controls cover normal accepted completion, changed/rearmed Yard preserved, and refused placement after replacement without any placement call, in both directions. Preflight/placement promises are controlled source ports; this is not actual native worker acceptance.

### Actual main timing and final queued fixture checkpoint

Actual main's async place callback calls commandSender.submit immediately and does not await a worker command ACK. The real native reproduction therefore holds placeAt's genuine preflight RESPONSE while changing renderer, then releases that unchanged response. Holding only the command ACK would not reproduce this production race.

Final source file also evaluates main's exact submission callback:14/14 GREEN. Both accepted-preflight renderer directions submit the exact original request and stand down; changed/rearmed selection before preflight resolution submits no old request. The unique disposed producer mutation gives4 RED /10 legal controls,576ms; exact corrected bytes restored14/14 GREEN,550ms. Related36/36 GREEN,721ms,maxWorkers2 and app/tools TypeScript GREEN.
